bio.tagline: Systems for AI, and AI for systems.
bio.summary: Final-year Electronics and Communication Engineering student at IIIT Hyderabad working on hardware/software co-design for AI: compute-in-memory circuits, accelerator architecture, and the ML systems that run on them.
long: I am an undergraduate researcher at CVEST, IIIT Hyderabad, advised by Dr. Priyesh Shukla. My main work is ProbSplat, a floating-gate compute-in-memory macro that evaluates Gaussian-mixture log-likelihoods directly as column current, presented at IEEE ISVLSI 2026.

Around that, I have explored ternary-weight (BitNet) LLM inference toward a multiplication-free accelerator, and I am now exploring hardware architectures for datacenter-scale computing in a collaborative project with Google Silicon.
I like working across the stack: circuits and processors on one side, transformers, optimizers and distributed systems on the other, and compilers in between.

experience.detail: Hardware/software co-design for AI, advised by Dr. Priyesh Shukla
bullets: Co-designed ProbSplat, a 6T floating-gate inverter-array compute-in-memory macro that evaluates 3-D Gaussian-mixture log-likelihoods as column current, with threshold-voltage programming that sets each Gaussian's mean and variance almost independently.
Mapped trained Gaussian-splatting scenes onto int8 precision with opacity pruning, and projected about 18 pJ per 4-bit inference from an ADC, DAC and array breakdown.

Explored ternary-weight (BitNet) LLM inference toward a multiplication-free accelerator; now exploring hardware architectures for datacenter-scale computing in a collaborative project with Google Silicon.
Cut ATE test time by about 50% by restructuring the C++ tester program to run independent test sequences in parallel.

Built Python pipelines over tester and bench logs for statistical test-limit guard-banding in Spotfire, combining variances in quadrature, and correlated tester and bench data across test insertions for a yield study.

publications.title: ProbSplat: Efficient Probabilistic Hardware for Gaussian Splatting in 3D Scene Reconstruction
publications.venue: IEEE Computer Society Annual Symposium on VLSI (ISVLSI)
publications.summary: A floating-gate inverter-array compute-in-memory macro that evaluates 3-D Gaussian-mixture log-likelihoods with programmable mean and variance, as a low-energy backend for Gaussian-splatting scene reconstruction.
publications.abstract: This paper presents ProbSplat, a Compute-in-Memory (CIM)-inspired architecture based on programmable and energy efficient floating-gate inverter columns for probabilistic computing. Improving upon our prior work, ProbSplat programs and stores both means and variances of Gaussian mixture components, and evaluates log-likelihood for gaussian splatting during scene reconstruction with high energy efficiency, suitable for robotics and augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR) at the edge. Our proposed scheme enables independent control of both mean and variance via deterministic adjustment of floating-gate MOSFET threshold voltages, increasing the fidelity of hardware to program probability distributions. The design is simulated in 180nm CMOS on 1.8 V at 50 MHz and achieves mean–variance independence with < 2.4% deviation during 3-D Gaussian mixture modeling. Compared to conventional digital implementations, ProbSplat significantly reduces compute complexity, memory footprint, and power consumption. The scalable framework consumes 18pJ energy per log-likelihood inference with 4-bit precision while operating for 500 mixture functions in a 3-D GMM. Scene reconstruction with ProbSplat's characteristics gave satisfactory fidelity of 21.99 PSNR (dB) at 8-bit precision.

projects.title: CLARITY: Unmasking Political Question Evasions
projects.one_liner: Classifying how clearly politicians answer interview questions, with a confidence-routed LLM cascade.
projects.context: SemEval-2026 Task 6; Advanced NLP course project, team of four
bullets: Built a classifier for how clearly politicians answer interview questions (SemEval-2026 Task 6, 9 evasion types), comparing LoRA-tuned Qwen3-8B against DeBERTa-v3 encoder variants in controlled ablations.

Added a confidence-routed cascade: a vLLM-served LLM picks among the classifier's candidate labels for only its least-confident items, distilled into a LoRA student that matches a 10-seed ensemble at 4.7x less GPU time.

key_numbers.label: less GPU time than a 10-seed ensemble

projects.title: Anatomy of a Language Model
projects.one_liner: Transformers, experts, optimizers and decoding, each built by hand in PyTorch and ablated one factor at a time.
bullets: Built encoder-decoder and decoder-only Transformers in PyTorch with swappable MHA/GQA attention, RoPE, RMSNorm, BPE and byte-level patching, and ablated one component at a time on a cipher-decryption task.

Implemented Mixture-of-Experts layers (top-k and shared-expert routing), optimizers such as Muon and AdEMAMix, and beam, top-k and top-p decoding over a KV cache; Muon reached AdamW's loss in half the tokens.

key_numbers.label: the tokens for Muon to reach AdamW's loss

projects.title: Scaling Log Analytics: Batch, Stream & Service
projects.one_liner: One server-log workload built three ways (MPI, MapReduce, gRPC streaming) to compare distributed-systems models.
bullets: Built one server-log analytics workload as a C++/MPI batch job, a MapReduce job and a gRPC streaming pipeline to compare how each model shapes communication and design; all three match a sequential reference exactly.

Kept MPI communication small via per-rank summaries and one top-K ranking after the merge (6.39x on 7 nodes); the gRPC pipeline (producer, coordinator, workers) applies backpressure and serves live queries mid-ingestion.

projects.title: Machine Learning Methods and Models
projects.one_liner: Classical ML through diffusion models, implemented and analysed notebook by notebook.
bullets: Implemented K-Means, Gaussian Mixture Models (EM) and PCA in NumPy, and applied KNN, decision trees, random forests and L1/L2 polynomial regression with validation-based tuning; used the GMM for satellite image segmentation.
Built an MLP with manual backpropagation for coordinate-based image reconstruction and autoencoder anomaly detection; trained CNNs, an RNN forecaster, VAEs and a U-Net diffusion model in PyTorch.

projects.title: IntelliStay: AI Churn Retention Platform
projects.one_liner: Predicts insurance churn, explains each customer's risk, and drafts the retention action, all on a local machine.
bullets: Built a churn pipeline for 336K auto-insurance customers: feature engineering, SMOTE on the training split, an XGBoost classifier, SHAP for per-customer risk drivers, and DiCE counterfactuals restricted to premium reductions.
Fed SHAP drivers and counterfactuals to a locally hosted LLM (Qwen3-4B) that drafts retention actions and nudge messages without customer data leaving the machine; won Megathon 2025.

projects.title: CIM-Based LLM Accelerator
projects.one_liner: A hybrid accelerator: systolic array for prefill, in-memory compute for memory-bound decode.
bullets: Designed a hybrid LLM-inference accelerator: a systolic array for compute-heavy prefill matrix multiplies, modeled in SystemC with output- and weight-stationary dataflows and tiling, reaching 4.4x fewer cycles.
Paired it with an 8T-SRAM in-memory-compute core for memory-bound decode, simulated in NGSpice, to reduce weight movement, which limits decode more than arithmetic.

projects.title: RISC-V Processor
projects.one_liner: A 5-stage pipelined core with forwarding, stalls and flushes, growing toward an out-of-order RV64I design.
bullets: Designed a RISC-V processor in Verilog with sequential and 5-stage pipelined (IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB) datapaths supporting add, sub, and, or, addi, ld, sd and beq, built from a control unit, ALU, register file and data memory.

Resolved pipeline hazards with EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding, load-use stalls and branch flushes; checked it in simulation with an assembler script and Fibonacci, vector-add, linear-search and 15 targeted hazard programs.

projects.title: Racket Compiler
projects.one_liner: A multi-pass Racket-to-x86 compiler with register allocation and a C runtime.
bullets: Built a multi-pass Racket-to-x86 compiler with IRs for integers, booleans, tuples, conditionals, loops and functions.
Implemented register allocation and dataflow analysis, linked a C runtime, and validated output with a test harness.

projects.title: 4-Bit Carry Lookahead Adder
projects.one_liner: From schematic to layout to FPGA: a CLA characterised in SPICE and verified in MAGIC.
bullets: Designed a 4-bit CLA, measured delay and power in NGSpice, verified its layout in MAGIC, tested on FPGA.
